Hi Samir and Leah,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the clarity on BlueCart's real‑time search & summarization use cases. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size Dedicated correctly:

Recap (from our side)
- Primary workloads: (1) user-initiated search/autocomplete (low latency, bursty), (2) nightly batch embedding updates (throughput-heavy), (3) on-demand summarization for enterprise customers (mixed token lengths).
- Data residency: must remain in AWS us-west-2 VPC.
- SLA target: 95th percentile < 180ms for search responses.

Questions we need answers to for sizing:
1) TPS targets for search at peak (requests/sec) and expected token-per-request (avg / 95th).
2) Summarization concurrency: how many simultaneous long-running summarizations do you expect (and avg tokens out)?
3) Batch embedding window size & target throughput (items/hour).

Attached is a lightweight capacity worksheet (bluecart_capacity_worksheet.csv) — can you fill the shaded columns? If easier, reply with ballpark numbers and we'll take that to Karthik for a recommended GPU mix.

Next steps:
- Samir/Leah: fill the worksheet or reply with estimates by EOD Thu.
- Internal: once we have numbers, Karthik will draft a Dedicated SKU recommendation and a short canary rollout plan.

Thanks —
Avery

Avery — thanks for the clear recap. Filling this out from our ops side (ballparks for now):

- Search/autocomplete (prod peak): ~220 req/s peak across the fleet. Avg tokens per request: 18 tokens. 95th: 60 tokens.
- Summarization (enterprise on-demand): expect 8 concurrent long jobs during business hours. Avg input ~1,800 tokens, output ~400 tokens. Jobs usually stream results; tail latency tolerance up to 3s but prefer <1s for first token.
- Nightly embeddings: ~1.2M docs per night; target throughput ~80k items/hour during batch window.

Other notes:
- We can tolerate a short warmup for KV cache on canary deploys but want predictable tail latency.
- We would prefer not to run on mixed-tenancy with other customers — Dedicated is a requirement unless Private VPC pricing is reasonable.

Hope this helps — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to validate assumptions.

Avery / team / Samir — quick sizing sketch based on the numbers below. I kept it conservative on latency and flexible for burst capacity. Attaching a short SKU plan (Dedicated_Sku_Plan_v1.xlsx).

Summary recommendation (first-pass):
- Search (low-latency): provision 6x A100-80GB-equivalent cards (dedicated pool) running optimized compiled kernels with continuous batching disabled for search routes; target per-GPU sustainable search throughput ~40-50 rps at 50-60 token 95th with 1-2 concurrent in-flight search requests per model replica. This hits ~240-300 rps headroom for autoscaling. Use aggressive prefix KV caching (per-customer cache with 30 minute TTL) to reduce token work for repeated queries.

- Summarization (long jobs): provision 2x H100-80GB-esque cards for heavy generation paths (long context). Each card can handle ~4 concurrent summarization streams at ~2k input tokens with mixed precision; run those on a separate pool to avoid queuing tail latency for search. Keep streaming enabled; configure token-budgeted batching (small internal batches of 2-4) to maximize throughput without hurting first-token latency.

- Embedding batch window: run ephemeral GPU-backed batch workers (can burst onto extra A100 capacity) — size for 80k/hr means ~22 embeddings/sec sustained; a single A100 can handle this with optimized kernels if batched; allocate an extra card for headroom during ingestion spikes.

Recommended configuration: 8x A100-equivalents + 2x H100-equivalents in us-west-2 Dedicated pool, with autoscale headroom of 2 additional A100s for peak days. Canary rollout plan: start with 50% traffic to Dedicated search pool, ramp over 24–48h, monitor 95th latency and token spend.

Operational knobs:
- Concurrency: search routes 1–2 in-flight per replica; summarization pool 3–4 concurrent per replica.
- Batching: search: continuous small-batch disabled; summarization: micro-batching (size 2–4).
- Caching: per-customer prefix KV cache + short-lived model-level cache for commonly requested completions.

Estimated commit band (guesstimate): $55–75k/month for reserved Dedicated pool with the above mix (depends on committed term and preferred GPU flavors). I will convert to a SKU-level quote after we confirm preferred GPU family (A100 vs newer Ampere refresh or H100-backed inference).

Next steps:
1) Samir/Leah: confirm tolerance for having all summarization jobs on a separate pool (yes/no).
2) Avery: if confirmed, I will produce a formal SKU + canary runbook and a short performance slide (24–36 hours).

Attachment: Dedicated_Sku_Plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub: sheets: sizing_summary, cost_estimate, rollout_runbook)
